=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_autofix_step_assemble_failure_evidence.sh: lines 13-17 and lines 56-66 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `failure-headline` and `autofix-failure-fingerprint` calls omit `--evidence-file "${RUNTIME_DIR:-}/sandbox_prepare_failure_evidence.txt"`.
  WHY: Sandbox-prepare failures lose their first-error detail and fingerprint evidence, potentially collapsing distinct failures into one fingerprint and affecting the identical-failure cap.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_assemble_failure_evidence.sh: lines 56-69 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `autofix-failure-fingerprint` call omits `--support-sha "${REVIEW_SUPPORT_SHA:-}"`.
  WHY: The resulting marker lacks its support SHA, so the gate, cap job, and sweep ignore it; severity disagreement: MAJOR and BLOCKER were reported, using BLOCKER.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: lines 5696-5704 and lines 5792-5821 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A failed review-blocked judge is classified as a provider outage based on the live OpenRouter probe without checking provider-error evidence from the judge.
  WHY: An unrelated judge failure during a provider outage can be mislabeled, causing real failures or review-blocked labels to be hidden or removed during recovery.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml; scripts/provider_outage.py: Workflow call at review_autofix.yml:4915; environment reads at provider_outage.py:850-853 and 262 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The review workflow does not export the documented `PROVIDER_OUTAGE_CLASSIFY_ENABLED` and `PROVIDER_OUTAGE_PROBE_MODEL` variables to the classifier process.
  WHY: Operators' configured kill switch and probe model do not affect review failure classification.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: `GitHub.dispatch()` method (~line 340) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `GitHub.dispatch()` passes `-f allow_workflow_edits=false` unconditionally.
  WHY: Resumed reviews disable workflow edits even when the regular sweep dispatch honours `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS`.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: `sweep()` (`if result.get("outcome") != "up": values["paused"] = "true"`) with `probe_openrouter()` returning "unknown" | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `sweep()` pauses review dispatches when the probe outcome is `unknown`, including when the key is missing or the probe has an inconclusive response.
  WHY: An inconclusive probe can leave reviews paused indefinitely without bounded escalation or an additional alert; severity disagreement: NIT and MAJOR were reported, using MAJOR.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: `open_tracker()` returning `{"outcome":"failed","alert":False}` and the `find_trackers() is None` branch of `sweep()` | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Tracker lookup or creation failures are swallowed, produce no alert, and can leave `sweep()` writing `paused=false`.
  WHY: A confirmed outage can remain untracked and unalerted while review dispatches continue and per-PR outage alerts are suppressed; severity disagreement: MAJOR and BLOCKER were reported, using BLOCKER.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: `open_tracker()` | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `open_tracker()` does not check whether `gh.comment(number, ...)` succeeds.
  WHY: If the tracker comment fails, the tracker may be opened without the intended outage notification.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: end of `sweep()` (`gh.comment(...)`, `gh.close_issue(...)`, then `values["recovered"]="true"` and the alert) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Recovery ignores the results of the recovery comment and tracker close, then reports recovery unconditionally.
  WHY: If closing the tracker fails, later ticks can repeat the recovery comment and alert; severity disagreement: MAJOR was reported, using MAJOR.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: close_tracker() | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `close_tracker()` logs a tracker-close failure but returns `closed`.
  WHY: Callers may treat the tracker as cleaned up and create duplicate outage tracker issues if another outage occurs immediately.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: lines 82-84 (import block) and line 90 (OUTAGE_COMMENT_HEADLINE constant) | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `workflow_failure_heal` is imported as `_wfh` and `OUTAGE_COMMENT_HEADLINE` is defined, but neither is used.
  WHY: Each CLI invocation eagerly imports a large module and incurs unnecessary startup cost.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: lines 4909-4923 (the inline provider-outage classification in the editor-empty-noop path) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The editor-empty-noop classification scans a narrower set of logs than the extracted failure-evidence step.
  WHY: Provider errors in resolver or collect-metadata stderr can be missed, causing an outage to be classified as `editor_empty` and counted toward the identical-failure cap.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_assemble_failure_evidence.sh: `export AUTOFIX_FAILURE_REASON=provider_unavailable`, followed by the `helper_failed` early `exit 0` before `$GITHUB_ENV` is written | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The outage classification is written to `$GITHUB_ENV` only after fingerprint processing, which the `helper_failed` early exit skips.
  WHY: If the fingerprint helper fails, later steps lose the outage reason and cannot write a marker or resume the PR.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: provider_failure_status at lines 175-202; classify at lines 271-278 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Classification treats any matching provider error in supplied logs as evidence that the current failure was caused by the provider.
  WHY: A recovered provider error in an earlier attempt combined with a failing probe can misclassify a separate editor or infrastructure failure.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: Lines 648-650 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: After dispatching PR reviews, resume ignores the result of `patch_body` when persisting dispatched PR numbers.
  WHY: A successful dispatch may not be recorded if the tracker update fails, allowing a later tick to dispatch the same PR again.
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py: `test_review_autofix_workflow_backfills_the_heal_reporter_from_main_snapshot` (~2691), `test_fingerprint_cap_log_prefixes_are_registered` (~3111), `test_review_autofix_passes_support_sha_to_every_marker_site` (~3635), `test_review_autofix_failure_comment_names_the_failed_step_and_first_error` (~4348) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Contract tests still read raw workflow YAML or expect the old reporter list and inline content after workflow bodies moved into scripts.
  WHY: The stale assertions fail in CI; severity disagreement: MAJOR and BLOCKER were reported, using BLOCKER.
- tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py: `test_identical_failure_fingerprint_marker_on_every_failure_comment` (~line 7849) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The test detects that the extracted failure-evidence script omits the sandbox-prepare evidence-file argument.
  WHY: The contract test fails and identifies the missing argument in the script.
- scripts/label_helpers.sh: `_AI_LABEL_COLORS` (around line 77) and the description catalog (around line 137), next to `ai:operator-step` | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `ai:provider-outage` is in `.github/ai/label_contract.v1.json` but missing from both label helper catalogs.
  WHY: The label-parity CI test fails, and helper-based label creation falls back to a generic color and description.
- tests/test_smoke_alert_silencing_contract.py: the `review_autofix.yml` expected declaration list (around lines 62-67) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The test pins four `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL` declarations although the workflow now has seven.
  WHY: The declaration-count assertion fails in CI.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py: `test_contract_helper_guard_in_poller_tests`, which failed in orchestrate-poll shard 0 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The poller contract test's expected helper staging set is stale after provider-outage support was added.
  WHY: The orchestrate-poll shard fails on the PR head.
- workflow-templates/ai-review.yml: job `provider-outage-resume`, step "Check out trusted provider-outage support" (`ref: stable`) | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The consumer job checks out coding-workflows at the moving ref `stable` rather than a release SHA.
  WHY: The helper can drift independently of the pinned workflow release.
- workflow-templates/ai-review.yml: lines 96-149 (the `provider-outage-resume` job, especially lines 101-109) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The scheduled consumer job checks out provider-outage support and calls its sweep without first checking for an outage tracker.
  WHY: Healthy consumers still incur checkout, fetch, and GitHub issues-list work on every scheduled tick.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: lines 3271-3292 (the "Record Claude pool capacity" step and the script it sources) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The capacity step also invokes the tracker close path when a Claude account is available, including on ordinary review runs.
  WHY: Consumer runs with Claude configured make an unnecessary tracker-list GitHub API call when no capacity tracker needs closing.
